study type: Mixed Methods (Quantitative: Retrospective Cohort; Qualitative: Explorative Study)
exposure: racial/ethnic bias (including stereotypes and assumptions) among maternal and newborn care professionals
outcome: maternal and perinatal outcomes (including uterine rupture and caesarean section frequency)
difference in the response time to pain
decision-making about pain assessment, management, and treatment
cohort: The study participants included womxn experiencing uterine rupture identified through the Netherlands Obstetric Surveillance System and maternal and newborn care professionals in the Netherlands.
finding: The study found that caesarean sections were performed significantly later for non-Western womxn experiencing pain, and care professionals exhibited both the presence and unawareness of racial/ethnic stereotypes influencing pain assessment and treatment.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was significantly more frequently performed after 180 minutes from the first complaint of pain in non-Western womxn compared to Western womxn.
